content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged brown bear frame. Host frame: the brown bear sets the outline, body size, and overall frame. A single creature combining a european rhinoceros beetle and a brown bear. The head is that of the brown bear, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: brown bear body and legs with dense fur on the face, plain coat, no stripes or spots; from the european rhinoceros beetle, as parts and materials on the brown bear's own body: a head horn grown from the frontal bone above and between the eyes, emerging from the covering which continues into the body covering of smooth, glossy dark cuticle, one horn curving upward and back from the head, long and curved; hard, glossy chitin plates with fine seams in its own colors, grown from the skin as the brown bear's own covering over the crown of the head, neck, shoulders, back, flanks, belly, hips, legs, and tail. It replaces the brown bear's dense fur there and conforms to the brown bear's body as a few large, smooth, fused plates, each spanning a whole body region of the brown bear (the shoulders, the back, the hips, each limb section), sized to the brown bear's body and joined by flexible cuticle at every joint. Every covered part keeps the brown bear's own length and shape, and the tail stays the brown bear's own tail; the dense fur stops at the covering's edge, and the face keeps the brown bear's own dense fur. The covering follows the body's own shape and bends at every joint. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs and rows of small breathing openings (spiracles) along the flanks. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws, and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

**Composing natural history illustration**
I'm assembling the hybrid with a bear head and fur, a long curved beetle horn, glossy chitin plates over the body and limbs, spiracles along the flanks, and a plain light background in a side three-quarter view.
**Refining unicorn illustration**
I'm adjusting the design to show a single horn as requested, then regenerating the image to match the user's specification.
